** EFI SYSTEM **

Bootloader install:
mkdir -p /boot/EFI/limine
cp /usr/share/limine/BOOT{X64,IA32}.EFI /boot/EFI/limine/

Bootloader EFI entry:
efibootmgr \
  --create \
  --disk /dev/sdX \
  --part Y \
  --label "sauzerOS Limine" \
  --loader '\EFI\limine\BOOT{X64,IA32}.EFI' \
  --unicode

** BIOS SYSTEM **
mkdir -p /boot/limine
cp /usr/share/limine/limine-bios.sys /boot/limine/
limine bios-install /dev/sdX (BIOS with MBR)
limine bios-install /dev/sdX partition_number (BIOS with GPT)

** CONFIGURATION **
limine.conf

timeout: 5

/sauzerOS
    protocol: linux
    path: boot():/vmlinuz-xxx
    cmdline: root=UUID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx rw
    module_path: boot():/initramfs-xxx.img

/Windows
    protocol: efi
    path: boot():/EFI/Microsoft/Boot/bootmgfw.efi


encrypted root example:
rd.luks.name=66426732-4215-4774-b341-74b055c233d7=rootfs root=/dev/mapper/rootfs rootflags=subvol=@

** SECURE BOOT (optional, EFI only) **
Needs sbctl. Nothing changes until its keys exist: limine-update, run by the
kernel and limine packages, only removes the entries of removed kernels.
Once keys exist it adds BLAKE2B hashes to the kernel and initramfs paths in
limine.conf, enrolls the config's hash into /boot/EFI/limine/*.EFI and
signs them. With Secure Boot on, Limine then refuses a changed config,
kernel or initramfs, and its menu editor is disabled.

1. Install Limine as above and boot with it, Secure Boot off.
2. Check that the firmware accepts new keys:
   sbctl status            (Setup Mode: Enabled)
   If not, clear the Secure Boot keys in the firmware setup first.
3. Create your keys:
   sbctl create-keys
4. Enroll them:
   sbctl enroll-keys --tpm-eventlog
   This trusts only your keys plus the option ROMs this machine loaded
   (a graphics card's). If sbctl refuses it, use instead:
   sbctl enroll-keys --microsoft
   which also trusts every Microsoft-signed boot loader.
5. Hash the files, enroll the config and sign Limine:
   limine-update
6. Check that Limine is signed:
   sbctl verify
7. Reboot into the firmware setup: enable Secure Boot and set a firmware
   password (otherwise anyone can turn Secure Boot off again).
8. Once booted:
   sbctl status            (Secure Boot: Enabled)
9. Back up /var/lib/sbctl offline: without the keys, the firmware has to be
   reset to setup mode to change anything.

Afterwards run limine-update after any change to limine.conf, and after
building a kernel or initramfs by hand (dracut): Limine refuses whatever no
longer matches its hash. The UEFI Shell entries do not boot with Secure Boot
on: they are unsigned on purpose, as a signed shell would bypass it.

To go back: turn Secure Boot off in the firmware, move /var/lib/sbctl
away, then run:
cp /usr/share/limine/BOOTX64.EFI /boot/EFI/limine/
limine-update
